## Back to Research Themes

Return to the [Research Themes and Experiment Ledger](experiment-ledger.{{< meta report-ext >}}).

## Technical summary

Quality-accepted Whisper large-v3 improved a selected ten-row lexical-speech
ablation from `4/10` to `7/10`, with three rescues and no observed degradation.
That supports a narrow lexical-speech route, not global transcript attachment
or multilingual robustness. Transcript provenance must remain visible:
automatic ASR, uploader captions, dataset recording-prompt references, and
independently produced human transcripts answer different questions.

## Why this theme matters

Speech evidence can resolve a visual ambiguity, but fluent text can still be
wrong, incomplete, translated from the wrong source, or supplied with a
misleading provenance label. A transcript comparison is interpretable only
when it holds frames, model, prompt, and decoding fixed and records how each
text was produced.

## Current working answer

Use quality-gated Whisper large-v3 as a **Routed candidate** for selected
lexical-speech questions, with a matched frame-only control. Do not treat its
acceptance rule as language recognition or fidelity. Keep the strict
independently produced human-transcript tier **Blocked** until independent
transcriber/reviewer records exist.

## What has been tried

### Transcript provenance tiers {#transcript-provenance-tiers}

Define the tiers before comparing them:

1. **automatic ASR output** — text generated by a specified ASR system from
   the frozen media;
2. **uploader caption** — text supplied by the uploader, with its own unknown
   authoring and alignment properties;
3. **dataset recording-prompt reference** — a dataset-supplied reference for
   the recording prompt, not evidence of an independent transcript review;
4. **independently produced human transcript** — a transcript with independent
   transcriber and reviewer provenance records.

No tier may be relabeled as another. In particular, a dataset
recording-prompt reference is not a TRECVID human oracle.

### Automatic transcript ablation {#automatic-transcript-ablation}

- **Reason for testing:** an early transcript changed an answer, but the
  project needed a label-blind matched test of accepted ASR on lexical speech.
- **Tested condition and panel:** identical 12-frame Qwen requests with and
  without a quality-accepted Whisper large-v3 transcript on ten selected
  lexical-speech rows; all 20 predictions froze before scoring.
- **Observed result:** manual accuracy changed from `4/10` to `7/10`, with
  three rescues and no observed degradation on that selected lexical-speech
  panel.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Routed candidate** for quality-gated
  lexical speech; not a global transcript default.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The selected ten-row diagnostic does not estimate routing prevalence, global
transcript value, non-lexical vocalization performance, or 2026 accuracy.
Transcript acceptance was mechanically label-blind; its validity is separate
from transcript fidelity. See the [automatic-transcript
report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/oracle_transcript_diagnostic_issue_7.md)
and its [frozen ablation plan](../../plans/issue-7-automatic-transcript-ablation.md).
</details>

### Multilingual and translation follow-ups {#multilingual-translation-followups}

- **Reason for testing:** determine whether the intended non-English-to-English
  ASR route was sufficiently evidenced for multilingual claims.
- **Tested condition and panel:** frozen-30 Whisper `task="translate"` on 30
  requests, plus follow-up research and a proposed language-stratified design;
  there was no human language/transcript reference panel.
- **Observed result:** 29 mechanically accepted outputs could be attached to
  matched requests, but the completed mixed panel lacked source-language labels
  and transcript/translation references.
- **Current condition-bound status:** compatibility evidence for the route;
  **not** multilingual robustness or transcript-fidelity evidence.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The Latin-script/rate gate can accept fluent but incorrect English, accept an
untranslated Latin-script language, and reject legitimate names or mixed
scripts. A proposed 30-clip multilingual diagnostic needs human-verified source
language, source transcript, and English translation, then matched visual-only
and Whisper conditions. See the [multilingual follow-up](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/multilingual_qwen36_followup_2026-07-24.md),
[ASR options](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/asr_model_followup_options_2026-07-20.md),
and [frozen-30 report](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/native_audio_model_benchmark_results_2026-07-21.md).
</details>

### Seamless diagnostic {#seamless-diagnostic}

- **Reason for testing:** countercheck Whisper translation on the difficult
  speech example with a different speech-to-text translation family.
- **Tested condition and panel:** one speech example with identical frozen
  12-frame Qwen evidence and a SeamlessM4T-v2 large transcript.
- **Observed result:** the English output was materially incomplete and the
  downstream answer remained wrong; relative to frames-only, token F1 and
  METEOR decreased.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Not promoted under the tested
  condition**; a one-example diagnostic, not an ASR accuracy estimate.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The reference was joined only after exact-capture inference. The output's
mechanical rule pass was not treated as semantic credibility: it omitted later
speech evidence needed for the answer. The result does not rule out another
language, model revision, panel, or independently verified translation route.
See the [Seamless follow-up](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/seamless_audio_followup_results_2026-07-21.md).
</details>

### External dataset-reference research {#external-dataset-reference-research}

- **Reason for testing:** specify a provenance-safe control that can compare
  automatic ASR against a dataset recording-prompt reference.
- **Tested condition and panel:** research design for a small external
  four-video, three-condition control; no TRECVID effectiveness result.
- **Observed result:** the design distinguishes frames-only, automatic-ASR,
  and dataset-reference text while freezing predictions before labels load.
- **Current condition-bound status:** an **Open hypothesis/design**, not a
  TRECVID human oracle or an effectiveness result.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

The external reference is a dataset-provided recording-prompt reference, not a
human transcriber/reviewer record. It must not pass a `human_verified_oracle`
validator or be called gold. The [external dataset-reference
research](../../reports/trecvid_vqa_2026/external_gold_transcript_benchmark_research_2026-07-24.md)
also specifies identical frames/model/prompt/decoding across conditions.
</details>

### Human-oracle tier {#human-oracle-tier}

- **Reason for testing:** estimate the upper bound from independently produced
  transcript evidence without leaking answer labels.
- **Tested condition and panel:** none yet; independent transcriber and
  reviewer records are absent.
- **Observed result:** no valid human-oracle result exists.
- **Current condition-bound status:** **Blocked** until independent provenance
  records and a label-blind protocol exist.

<details>
<summary>Method, result, validity risks, and evidence</summary>

Uploader captions, ASR ensembles, and dataset references cannot substitute for
this tier. A true upper bound needs independent transcript production and
review, immutable provenance, matching downstream controls, and answer labels
loaded only after prediction freeze.
</details>

## What the evidence supports

- On the selected ten lexical-speech rows, accepted Whisper changed manual
  accuracy from 4/10 to 7/10, with three rescues and no observed degradation.
- Transcript output can be included in a label-isolated request path while a
  rejected output becomes null.
- Fluent or mechanically accepted translation is not by itself faithful audio
  evidence; the Seamless diagnostic shows this distinction.
- Dataset recording-prompt references can be a separately labeled control, not
  a TRECVID human-oracle result.

## What it does not rule out

- The ten-row ablation does not establish global transcript use, route
  prevalence, multilingual effectiveness, or effects on non-lexical sound.
- The multilingual follow-up does not identify source languages or translation
  fidelity in frozen-30.
- The one-row Seamless result does not reject all alternative or multilingual
  ASR systems.
- The blocked human tier does not imply a zero upper bound; it means no valid
  upper-bound evidence exists yet.

## Possible bugs, confounds, and audit gaps

- **Uncertainty:** selected lexical-speech rows are diagnostic rather than a
  prevalence or global-accuracy sample.
- **Uncertainty:** the rate/Latin-script acceptance policy is not a language
  detector, an accuracy measure, or a human transcript review.
- **Audit gap:** no human source-language transcript or faithful translation
  reference is available for the completed multilingual route.
- **Blocked prerequisite:** the strict human tier lacks independent
  transcriber/reviewer provenance records; other text tiers must not fill that
  gap by renaming.

## Open hypotheses and ideas

- A prompt requiring timestamps and evidence spans may convert accepted lexical
  ASR into more grounded downstream answers than the current prompt.
- A label-blind human transcript can distinguish audio-evidence limits from
  ASR limits, but only if its provenance is independent.
- Alternative/multilingual ASR might help a declared stratum when compared on
  an identical frozen panel with explicit null and rejection controls.

## Cheapest valid next experiments

### Transcript grounding prompt

- **Hypothesis:** accepted Whisper plus a required timestamp/evidence-span
  grounding prompt improves lexical-speech answers over accepted Whisper with
  the current prompt.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** the existing accepted lexical-speech
  rows or a newly frozen matched subset, with both transcript prompts.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** same accepted Whisper output,
  frames, model, decoding, and question; retain a frame-only/null control;
  freeze all answers before labels and record the cited span.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** advance the grounding prompt only if a
  predeclared paired improvement occurs without degradation versus current
  accepted Whisper and controls.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** it would establish a
  prompt effect on that accepted-ASR panel, not transcript fidelity or global
  speech routing.

### Label-blind human-transcript upper bound

- **Hypothesis:** independently produced human transcripts reveal the maximum
  downstream value of faithful transcript evidence on a declared speech panel.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a small frozen speech-critical panel
  with independent transcriber and reviewer records and explicit provenance.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** label-blind transcript work;
  same frames/model/prompt/decoding for frame-only, ASR, and human conditions;
  immutable provenance; and answer labels loaded only after all predictions
  freeze.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** interpret the human-minus-ASR and
  human-minus-frames deltas only if provenance and independent review records
  are complete for every included row.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** it would be an upper
  bound for the declared panel, not a TRECVID-wide oracle or a substitute for
  independently verified 2026 evaluation.

### Alternative or multilingual ASR matched panel

- **Hypothesis:** an alternative or multilingual ASR can improve a declared
  speech stratum without hidden changes to the downstream visual pathway.
- **Smallest valid panel or work item:** a matched frozen panel with declared
  source-language/speech strata, including explicit no-speech, rejection, and
  null controls.
- **Matched controls and integrity safeguards:** same downstream frames,
  model, prompt, decoding, panel identities, and scoring; record ASR model,
  revision, language behavior, timestamps, acceptance/rejection, and nulls.
- **Decision or promotion rule:** advance only if the alternative meets its
  predeclared paired improvement and control non-regression criteria against
  current accepted Whisper.
- **Boundary on what a positive result would establish:** it would support the
  tested ASR on that frozen stratum, not multilingual robustness everywhere.
